claims.evidence: The witness report identifies all 21 cases as having the PS5 logo on the spine.
The witness report does not mention factory seals, and the discs themselves were not shown.
The witness identifies the items as PS5 games; the PlayStation 6 has not been released.

risks.proof: A continuous video clip showing each case being opened to reveal the corresponding disc.

risks.risk: The discs may be heavily scratched or unreadable.
risks.proof: Clear, high-resolution photos of the data side of every disc.

risks.risk: Games may be from a region incompatible with the buyer's account or DLC needs.
risks.proof: Photos of the back of the cases showing the region rating (ESRB, PEGI, etc.) or region code.
risks.if_unproven: as the least valuable regional variant.

proof_requests: Video of all 21 cases being opened to show the discs inside.
Close-up photos of the underside of the discs to check for scratches.
Photos of the back of the cases to verify game regions.
A photo of the items next to a piece of paper with today's date and the buyer's name to verify possession.
response.reason: The seller's description is fundamentally disconnected from the items shown, claiming they are PS4 games and a non-existent 'Ps6' model, which is a common indicator of a scam using stolen photos.
